Rooms.Name: The Title Page
Rooms.Description:
Welcome to "Nursery Rhymes for Children and the Young at Heart." 
This book will take you through the world of nursery rhymes and
children's songs.  Each page may only be visted once each time you
read this book so that you will not wear out the pages!  Make sure
you "look" at each page you visit so you can actually read the
rhymes.  Please go north to start reading.

Rooms.Name: The Table of Contents
Rooms.Description:
This book contains several nursery rhymes, all in alphabetical
order (we want our children to know their ABC's!).  To see a complete
listing, please "look" at this page.  You may go north to start
reading the rhymes. Enjoy!

ExtraDescriptions.Description:

Rooms.Name: The Farmer in the Dell
Rooms.Description:
The sounds and smells of farm life overwhelm your senses as you
wander into this page.  A large group of farmhands stand watching as
the farmer, his family, and all the animals dance around merrily. 
You can take a few minutes to join in the festivities, or you can
wander on to the next page to the north.

The farmer in the dell,

The cow takes a dog.

The dog takes a cat,

The cat takes a rat,
The cat takes a rat,

The cat takes a rat.

The rat takes the cheese,
Hi-ho, the derry-o,
The rat takes the cheese.

The cheese stands alone,
The cheese stands alone,
Hi-ho, the derry-o,
The cheese stands alone.

Rooms.Name: Georgie Peorgie
Rooms.Description:
A calliope plays in the background as you wander through this
page.  You appear to have wandered into a small town faire, complete
with clowns and circus animals.  A small group of boys stands here
laughing and playing midway games.  You can stay here a while to join
them, or wander on to the next page to the north.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
Georgie Peorgie, puddin' and pie,
Kissed the girls and made them cry.
When the boys came out to play,
Georgie Peorgie ran away.

Rooms.Name: Hickory Dickory Dock
Rooms.Description:
A large clock stands in the center of this small room, poised just
seconds before one o'clock.  The room appears to be the foyer of a
pleasant farm house that has been overrun by rodents!  You can stare
at the clock all day, or you can visit the next page to the north.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
Hickory, dickory, dock,
The mouse ran up the clock.
The clock struck one,
The mouse ran down!
Hickory, dickory, dock.

Rooms.Name: Hot Cross Buns
Rooms.Description:
It appears that you have wandered into a small bakery.  The scents
of cakes and pies fill your nostrils, making you ever so hungry!  You
can stay here and inhale the wonderful odors, or you can check out
the next page by going north.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
Hot cross buns!
Hot cross buns!
One a penny, two a penny,
Hot cross buns! 

Hot cross buns!
Hot cross buns!
If you have no daughters,
Give them to your sons!

Rooms.Name: The House that Jack Built
Rooms.Description:
This is the house that Jack built.  It doesn't look very sturdy,
as if Jack is not the best craftsman, but it is cozy and warm.  You
can stay a while if Jack doesn't mind, or you can visit the next page
by moving north.

Rooms.Name: Humpty Dumpty
Rooms.Description:
A large stone wall dominates this page.  Several distraught
soldiers stand around holding pieces of what appears to be a very
large egg.  Some of the pieces are scattered around on the ground,
and you are just a little surprised to see pieces of clothing mixed
in with them!  Oh no, what could have happened here?  You may attempt
to help the soldiers with whatever it is they are doing, or wander on
to another page to the north.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
Humpty Dumpty sat on a wall.
Humpty Dumpty had a great fall.
All the king's horses and all the king's men
Couldn't put Humpty together again!

Rooms.Name: It's Raining, It's Pouring
Rooms.Description:
Didn't you ever have one of those rainy days when you just wanted
to curl back up and go to sleep?  This page holds a nice warm bed,
right next to a large picture window.  As you look through the
window, you can see a torrential downpour.  You can stay here and
watch the rain fall, or you can move north to the next page.

Rooms.Name: Jack and Jill Went Up the Hill
Rooms.Description:
A large hill takes up most of this page.  It looks quite steep,
and you may want to watch your step if you decide to climb it!  A
small well, which appears to be a source of water for a nearby town,
stands at the top of the hill.  You may stay here and guard the well
for the townsfolk, or you can wander north to the next page.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
Jack and Jill
Went up the hill
To fetch a pail of water.
Jack fell down
And broke his crown
And Jill came tumbling after.

Up Jack got
And home did trot
As fast as he could caper
Went to bed
And plastered his head
With vinegar and brown paper.

Rooms.Name: Jack, Be Nimble
Rooms.Description:
This page appears to be set at a wonderful party.  People are
clapping and dancing as several young men attempt to show off their
agility and skill (at something!).  A shy young lady smiles at you as
you watch the crowd.  You can stay here and join in the fun, or you
can wander off to the next page to the north.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
Jack, be nimble,
Jack, be quick,
Jack, jump over
The candlestick.

Rooms.Name: Jack Sprat
Rooms.Description:
A banquet of royal proportions has been laid out upon a large
table on this page.  The food looks and smells quite delicious, and
you are tempted to have a little taste.  If you stay here too long,
your mouth will probably water enough to ruin this page, so you
should probably be on your way to the next page to the north.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
Jack Sprat could eat no fat,
His wife could eat no lean,
And so betwixt the two of them
They licked the platter clean

Rooms.Name: Knick, Knack, Paddy Whack
Rooms.Description:
The front porch of a small country home dominates most of this
page.  A cozy swing rocks gently in the breeze, and you hear a
rooster crowing in the distance.  You can watch this idyllic scene as
long as you'd like, or you can wander on to the next page to the
north.

Rooms.Name: Kookaburra
Rooms.Description:
This page appears to be set in a small forest.  A large gum tree
stands in the center of the page, filled with delicious gumdrops! 
You can hear an eerie laughing in the distance, but for some reason
you don't feel very afraid.  If you'd like to try and get some
gumdrops, you can stay on this page, but it might be nice to see
what's on the next page to the north.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
Kookaburra sits in the old gum tree.
Merry, merry king of the bush is he.

Laugh, Kookaburra,

Laugh, Kookaburra,
Gay your life must be. 

Kookaburra sits in the old gum tree,
Eating all the gumdrops he can see.

Stop, Kookaburra,

Stop, Kookaburra,
Leave some there for me.

Rooms.Name: Little Bo Peep
Rooms.Description:
This page is set in a large pasture.  The rolling hills smell of
sweet grass, which is just perfect for grazing sheep.  However, there
don't seem to be any sheep around!  You can stay here to wait for the
sheep to come by, or head north to the next page.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
Little Bo Peep has lost her sheep,
and doesn't know where to find them!
Let them alone, and they'll come home,
wagging their tails behind them!

Rooms.Name: Little Bunny Foo Foo
Rooms.Description:
This page is set in a lovely forest.  The tall trees stand
majestically over you, and the air is filled with the scent of pine. 
This forest is a magical place, filled with fairies and field mice! 
You may stay here and enjoy the scenery, or move on to the next page
to the north.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
Little Bunny Foo Foo
hoppin' through the forest,
scoopin' up the field mice
and boppin' em on the head. 

And down came the Blue Fairy, and she said: 
Little Bunny Foo Foo
I don't want to see you
scoopin' up the field mice
and boppin' em on the head. 
And now I'll give you three chances, and if you keep it up, 
I'll turn you into a goon. 

Little Bunny Foo Foo
kept hoppin' through the forest,
kept scoopin' up the field mice
and boppin' em on the head. 

And down came the Blue Fairy, and she said:

Little Bunny Foo Foo

scoopin' up the field mice

I'll turn you into a goon. 

Little Bunny Foo Foo
kept hoppin' through the forest,
kept scoopin' up the field mice
and boppin' em on the head. 

And down came the Blue Fairy, and she said: 
Little Bunny Foo Foo
I don't want to see you
scoopin' up the field mice
and boppin' em on the head. 
You disobeyed me three times, so now I'm gonna turn you into a GOON!

Rooms.Name: London Bridge is Falling Down
Rooms.Description:
A large bridge spanning a wide river stands in the middle of this
page.  The bridge appears to be crumbling, and in great need of
repair.  Perhaps you can help, or you can visit the next page by
going north.

Rooms.Name: The Man in the Moon
Rooms.Description:
The moon shines brightly upon you as you wander into this page. 
The night sky is filled with stars, and you are starting to feel just
a little sleepy. Perhaps you should move along to the next page
before you fall alseep!

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
The man in the moon
Looked out of the moon 
And this is what he said,
"Tis time that, now I'm getting up,
All babies went to bed."

Rooms.Name: Mary Had a Little Lamb
Rooms.Description:
A small country schoolyard takes up most of this page.  Children
are laughing and playing in the yard.  A small group is standing in a
circle giggling and pointing at something.  You can stay here to find
out what they are pointing at, or move north to the next page.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
Mary had a little lamb,
little lamb,
little lamb.
Mary had a little lamb,
Its fleece was white as snow. 

Everywhere that Mary went,
Mary went,
Mary went.
Everywhere that Mary went,
The lamb was sure to go. 

It followed her to school one day,
school one day,
school one day.
It followed her to school one day,
Which was against the rules. 

It made the children laugh and play,
laugh and play,
laugh and play.
It made the children laugh and play,
To see a lamb at school

Rooms.Name: Mary, Mary, Quite Contrary
Rooms.Description:
A beautiful garden, filled with flowers, dominates this page.  This
garden appears to be quite bountiful, with silver bells, and
cockleshells, and pretty maids all in a row.  You can stay here to
smell the flowers, or move on the the next page to the north.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
Mary, Mary, quite contrary,
How does your garden grow?
With silver bells and cockleshells,
And pretty maids all in a row.

Rooms.Name: Michael Row the Boat Ashore
Rooms.Description:
A deep, wide river flows down the middle of this page.  In the
center of the river is a small boat.  On one side of the river is a
large desert, and on the other side is a large oasis.  You can stay
here to see which side the boat is going to, or you can visit the
next page to the north.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
Michael, row the boat ashore,
Hallelujah.
Michael, row the boat ashore,
Hallelujah. 

Sister, help to trim the sails,
Hallelujah.
Sister, help to trim the sails,
Hallelujah. 

River Jordan's deep and wide,
Hallelujah.
Milk and honey on the other side,
Hallelujah. 

River Jordan's chilly and cold,
Hallelujah.
Chills the body, but warms the soul,
Hallelujah.

Rooms.Name: My Bonnie Lies Over the Ocean
Rooms.Description:
You are on a large dock at the edge of wide and stormy sea.  The
clouds above you are just starting to turn dark, when a gust of wind
blows a woman's handkerchief right to your feet.  Perhaps you'd like
to stay here to find out who the owner of the handkerchief is, or
perhaps you'd just like to get out of the rain and head north to the
next page.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
My Bonnie lies over the ocean,
My Bonnie lies over the sea.
My Bonnie lies over the ocean,
Please bring back my Bonnie to me.

Bring back,
Bring back,
Oh, bring back my Bonnie to me, to me.
Bring back,
Bring back,
Oh, bring back my Bonnie to me.

Rooms.Name: Old King Cole
Rooms.Description:
A large party in a beautifully decorated reception room fills this
page. You can only guess by the rich tapestries and colorful
paintings that the room belongs in the home of a man of taste.  A
group of lovely ladies stand along one wall, preparing to dance with
the young men of the kingdom.  You may join the festivities, or
continue on your way to the next page to the north.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
Old King Cole was a merry old soul,
And a merry old soul was he.
He called for his pipe, and he called for his bowl,
And he called for his fiddlers three.

Every fiddler had a fiddle fine,
And a very fine fiddle had he, had he.
Tweedle dum, tweedle dee, went the fiddlers three,
Tweedle dum dee, dum dee deedle dee.

Tweedle dum, tweedle dee, went the fiddlers three,
Tweedle dum dee, dum dee deedle dee.

Rooms.Name: Old Mother Hubbard
Rooms.Description:
This page is set in a small cottage.  A large cupboard stands
empty at the edge of the page.  The wooden floors are covered with
dirt, making you want to head to the next page which lies north.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
Old Mother Hubbard
Went to the cupboard
To fetch her poor dog a bone;
But when she came there
The cupboard was bare,
And so the poor dog had none.

She took a clean dish
To get him some tripe;
But when she came back
He was smoking a pipe.
She went to the grocer's
To buy him some fruit;
But when she came back
He was playing the flute.

She went to the baker's
To buy him some bread;
But when she came back
The poor dog was dead.

She went to the undertaker's
To buy him a coffin;
But when she came back
The poor dog was laughing.

She went to the hatter's
To buy him a hat;
But when she came back
He was feeding the cat.

The dame made a curtsey,
The dog made a bow;
The dame said, "Your servant."
The dog said, "Bow wow!"

Rooms.Name: On Top of Spaghetti
Rooms.Description:
Mmmmm, spaghetti!  This page is filled to the brim with
mouth-watering spaghetti.  Pasta and sauce are everywhere, and
everything smells simply divine.  You may leave this delectable page
by heading north.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
On top of spaghetti,
All covered with cheese,
I lost my poor meatball
When somebody sneezed. 

It rolled off the table
And onto the floor,
And then my poor meatball
Rolled right out the door!

Rooms.Name: One, Two, Buckle My Shoe
Rooms.Description:
A small child stands in the center of this page, learning how to
count to twenty.  In order to achieve this goal, he is learning a
simple rhyme to help him remember his numbers.  If you're not up to
learning how to count, just go north to the next page.

Rooms.Name: Over the River and Through the Woods
Rooms.Description:
The crisp cold air bites your nose as you wander through a wintery
scene.  You hear the tinkle of sleighbells somewhere in the distance,
and you can smell the warmth of a fire somewhere close by.  You can
enjoy this winter wonderland for a bit longer, or head north to the
next page.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
Over the river and through the woods,
to grandmother's house we go.
The horse knows the way
to carry the sleigh
through the white and drifty snow.
Oh! Over the river and through the woods,
to grandmother's house we go!

Rooms.Name: The End of the Book
Rooms.Description:
The book of nursery rhymes has come to an end.  As you turn the
last page, you wish you could have stayed a bit longer.  Don't fret
however, this book can always be checked out again!  Simply go north
to leave the book, or stay here to rest up a bit.

Mobs.Name: farmer
Mobs.LongDescription: The farmer smiles happily as he dances a jig.
Mobs.Description:
The farmer smells of sweat and manure, but he appears to be happy
enough.  His overalls look like they haven't been washed in weeks,
and you fear that standing too close to him may very well make you
pass out!

Mobs.Name: pig
Mobs.LongDescription: Strange, but true, this pig is dancing!
Mobs.Description:
This little fellow has pink skin, which has been covered almost
completely in mud.  He smells terrible, but he has the cutest little
face, and boy can he dance!

Mobs.Name: georgie peorgie boy
Mobs.LongDescription: Georgie Peorgie puckers up to give you a big wet kiss!
Mobs.Description:
Georgie Peorgie is quite the lady's man, but he doesn't seem to care
too much to let his playmates know.  He's short and stout, probably
from eating too much pie.  His dirty blonde hair is unkempt and could
probably use a good washing.

Mobs.Name: mouse
Mobs.LongDescription: A small mouse runs up the clock.
Mobs.Description:
The small mouse has a soft grey coat and long black whiskers.  His
giant ears look rather comical atop his tiny little head.  He stares
at you, twitching his tiny little tail.

Mobs.Name: baker
Mobs.LongDescription: The baker stands here, working magic on a piece of dough.
Mobs.Description:
The baker is an enormous man, who has an almost perfectly round
shape.  You imagine he probably got that way from eating a few too
many of his delicious baked goods.

Mobs.Name: jack man
Mobs.LongDescription: Jack smiles proudly at his handiwork.
Mobs.Description:
Jack stands tall in his dusty overalls.  His hair is covered with
sawdust and bits of wood.  He considers himself to be a master
builder, but one look at his handiwork and you know better!

Mobs.Name: old man
Mobs.LongDescription: An old man snores loudly as he sleeps the day away.
Mobs.Description:
This old man looks like he's had a rough time.  He has a huge bump on
his head, and he's snoring loud enough to wake the dead!  Might not
be a good idea to wake him, he doesn't look much like a morning
person.

Mobs.Name: jack boy
Mobs.LongDescription: A young boy carries his pail to the top of the hill.
Mobs.Description:
Jack is a handsome young fellow, full of energy and life.  He better
watch his step though, the steep hill looks quite treacherous.  Jack
probably wouldn't take too well to falling down!

Mobs.Name: jill girl
Mobs.LongDescription: Singing happily, a young girl climbs the steep hill.
Mobs.Description:
Jill is a pretty young girl, with smiling blue eyes and golden hair.
She appears to be walking a bit too quickly, and she better be
careful that she doesn't come tumbling down on her pretty little
head!

Mobs.Name: jack man
Mobs.LongDescription: A young man runs around with his pants on fire!
Mobs.Description:
Uh oh!  It seems that Jack got a little too close to the flame as he
jumped over the candlestick!  His pants are on fire, and he's
frantically trying to put them out.

Mobs.Name: jack sprat man husband
Mobs.LongDescription: An extremely thin man sits at the table, eating only the lean.
Mobs.Description:
Jack Sprat must eat no fat, he's ever so thin indeed!  His long, lean
frame appears almost skeletal.  Jack better start eating something
other than the lean, or he'll waste away to nothing.

Mobs.Name: wife jack sprat woman
Mobs.LongDescription: A portly, yet pretty, woman sits at the table stuffing her face.
Mobs.Description:
Jack Sprat's wife eats just about anything she can get her hands on,
and it certainly shows.  She's about four times the size of her
rail-thin husband.  Luckily for her (and for Jack) she's as pretty as
she is large.

Mobs.Name: kookaburra bird
Mobs.LongDescription: A large bird sits in the tree, eating all the gumdrops he can see.
Mobs.Description:
The kookaburra is a strange-looking bird, with a laugh to match.  He
sits high in the tree, eating all the tasty gumdrops.  Better hope he
saves some for you!

Mobs.Name: little bo peep girl
Mobs.LongDescription: A young girl stands crying in the pasture.
Mobs.Description:
Poor Little Bo Peep!  She fell asleep beneath a cozy tree, and her
sheep all wandered off.  Now she'll have to go home and explain that
to her parents.

Mobs.Name: little bunny foo
Mobs.LongDescription:
Laughing wildly, a small bunny picks up a field mouse and BOPS it on
the head!
Mobs.Description:
With his long ears and wiggly nose, Little Bunny Foo Foo looks
innocent enough, but one look in his eyes and you know this rabbit is
a maniac!  He takes joy in that pain of field mice - what a sicko!

Mobs.Name: mary girl
Mobs.LongDescription: A young girl plays with her classmates.
Mobs.Description:
Mary is a pretty young girl, wearing a frilly pink dress with
matching petticoat.  Her curly brown hair and big green eyes seem to
complete the picture.  What you can't tell from her appearance, is
that Mary has a thing for young sheep!

Mobs.Name: mary contrary gardener lady
Mobs.LongDescription: Tending to her garden, the young lady doesn't even notice you.
Mobs.Description:
Mary is quite the gardener.  She can grow anything almost anywhere,
and she's won numerous awards from the local gardening club.  Humming
softly to herself, she tends her magnificent garden.

Mobs.Name: michael boy
Mobs.LongDescription: A young boy is rowing across the river as fast as he can.
Mobs.Description:
Michael is very much the athlete, and he often rows himself across
the river to keep in shape.  This time however, he's rowing across
the river to see what he can of the promised land.

Mobs.Name: old king cole man
Mobs.LongDescription: Old King Cole watches over the festivities, chewing on his pipe.
Mobs.Description:
Old King Cole is a handsome old man, with twinkling grey eyes and a
perpetual smile.  He's dressed in the finest clothing available, and
while he has a bit of a belly, his outfit fits him quite well.

Objects.Name: wall
Objects.Description: A large stone wall spans the page.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
The stone wall is covered with moss.  Bits of eggshell and large
amounts of yolk are stuck to the large stones that make up the wall.

Objects.Name: swing
Objects.Description: The large swing rocks gently, inviting you to sit down and relax.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
The large swing is painted white to match the picket fence that
surrounds the small house.  It looks quite cozy, and would probably
make a great place to sit down and relax.

Objects.Name: gumdrop
Objects.Description: A tasty gumdrop seems to have fallen from the tree.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
This tasty morsel looks good enough to eat!  Better get it fast
before the Kookaburra snatches it up.

Objects.Name: brick
Objects.Description: An enormous brick has fallen from the bridge.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
This large brick was once part of the magnificent bridge.  However,
due to terrible maintenance, the bridge is falling apart.  The brick
looks quite heavy, and you probably won't be able to pick it up.

Objects.Name: moonbeam beam
Objects.Description: The moon reaches down and gently caresses you with a moonbeam.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
The soft light of the moonbeam lights up the room, but at the same
time makes you feel quite sleepy.

Objects.Name: bunch flower flowers
Objects.Description: A bunch of freshly-picked flowers rests on the edge of the garden.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
The delicious scent of the flowers fills your nose as you inhale
deeply.  Oh no!  You just inhaled a bug!  That'll teach you to go
around sniffing strange flowers!

Objects.Name: meatball
Objects.Description: A rather large meatball rolls off the spaghetti and onto the floor.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
This meatball is making your mouth water.  If it wasn't for the bits
of dust that it has aquired from being on the floor, it'd be
absolutely perfect!

Objects.Name: shoe
Objects.Description: Covered with mud, a small shoe sits here without his mate.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
The shoe is covered with mud, and it looks quite alone without its
mate.  A small silver buckle covers the top half of the shoe, and the
leather tongue seems to be sticking out right at you!  You better not
try to take the shoe, it looks quite stuck to the ground.
